capabilities: Chat with a local CodeBuddy CLI or Hermes agent from a sidebar or editor tab
Reference notes, files, MCP servers and subagents via @ mentions
Approve or reject Write/Edit/Bash/MCP tool calls through in-bubble approval cards
Show line-level diffs of agent edits and undo vault changes with one click
Manage MCP servers, subagents, sessions and installed skills from the UI
extras: Desktop only (Windows/macOS, no Linux), requires Obsidian 1.7.2+. README documents extensive limits and open issues, e.g. the WorkBuddy native path buffers output (~50s, ~640 KiB per request) rather than streaming token-by-token, Windows support is unverified, and Issue #10 stays open; install also possible via BRAT or manual release files.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to drive a local AI agent CLI, so users must switch to a terminal or external app to chat with, or let an agent edit, their notes.
